Done implementing. Nothing has been run or tested, per your request — this is code + design for review.

## What I built

A two-stage, resumable pipeline replicating the **Section 2 distress-elicitation** result, scoped to **Gemma-3-27B-it, Gemma-3-12B-it, Gemini-2.5-Flash, Gemini-2.5-Pro**:

```
distress_eval/
  prompts.py      # verbatim Appendix B: puzzles, triggers, tones, rejections, judge prompt
  config.py       # model + category registry (paper counts: 2000/400/600/200/800 = 4000)
  providers.py    # pluggable backends: OpenRouter / local-HF / Anthropic / Google
  wildchat.py     # 20 WildChat prompts from HF dataset, with fixed fallback
  elicitation.py  # build conversation plans + run multi-turn reject-and-rescore rollouts
  judge.py        # 0–10 frustration scoring (Claude Sonnet 4) + robust JSON parsing
  runner.py       # orchestrate generate→judge, JSONL persistence, resume
  analyze.py      # Figures 1/2/3 + Table 3 (differential words), JSON/CSV/plots
  cli.py          # generate | judge | run | analyze, --profile smoke
```
Plus `DESIGN.md`, `README.md`, `requirements.txt`.

## Key decisions (full rationale in DESIGN.md)

- **Inference backend**: the AskUserQuestion UI was dismissed, so I defaulted to the most flexible option — **OpenRouter for everything** (no GPU needed) with **paper-faithful local Gemma one flag away** (`--gemma-backend hf_local`). I flagged the caveat that OpenRouter may serve quantized Gemma, which matters for a behavioural propensity like this — so the headline Gemma numbers should be confirmed with the local backend. Easy to flip.
- **The biggest interpretive gap I had to resolve**: the paper's "4000 responses" vs the WildChat "20×40=800" tell. I concluded the per-category counts are **rollouts (conversations)**, judge **every turn**, and made the headline aggregation (`all` vs `final` turn) a documented config flag defaulting to `all`.
- **Other filled gaps** (each isolated and overridable): exact 20 WildChat prompts (load real ones / fallback), rejection phrasing pools, even rollout distribution across sub-conditions, judge temperature (0 for determinism), 2048 max tokens to capture score-9/10 collapses.
- **Faithful**: verbatim puzzle/judge/tone text, temperature 1, ≥5 threshold, `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, thinking disabled, exact model IDs.

DESIGN.md §4–5 catalogue every deviation and gap; §7 lists what a reviewer should re-check (local-vs-OpenRouter Gemma, WildChat prompt mismatch, headline granularity, the un-run GPT-5-mini judge cross-validation).

A couple of things worth your call before any run: whether you want me to switch the Gemma default to `hf_local` (if you have the GPUs and want paper-faithful weights), and whether the headline should aggregate `all` turns or `final`-only. Both are flags — let me know and I'll set the defaults accordingly. When you're ready, `run --profile smoke` is the intended first execution to validate wiring cheaply.
